# Panorama chunks use absolute ranges into one accumulated result array

The original incremental selection removes limit/offset fetching. Its listener accumulates messages in one array and sends inclusive absolute index ranges once unsent rows meet the configured threshold. The result-set loop can add more than the threshold, so the preference is not an exact chunk size. Successful completion sends the remainder before resolving the accumulated array; cancellation and errors reject first. The adapter indexes messages using the absolute range and invalidates those rows. In-group queries pass no chunk listener and still complete through their Promise. Accepted source retains these narrow contracts; no benchmark or query-race result is implied.

Scope: Panorama incremental LiveView selection.
